title: Find items by exact title
lead: Provide deterministic title equality for client-side dedupe while retaining ordinary substring search.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** making titles unique, fuzzy search changes, key-based filing, or title normalization.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: U4's workaround filters find results in a script. cmd_find currently casefolds and substring-matches fields. Exact matching is a small independent read-only capability.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: CLI find parser/handler, find tests, command and agent references, and CHANGELOG.md.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Exact mode returns a case-sensitive equal stored title; a superstring, different case, different Unicode normalization, and short-title-only match are excluded.
- Multiple identical stored titles return all matches in normal stable find order; done/retired inclusion follows existing find behavior.
- No match succeeds with the usual empty-result text and JSON shape.
- Exact mode combined with a positional substring query or --in fails as usage. Existing positional find behavior and output contracts are unchanged.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Add title-exact with its own TITLE argument, mutually exclusive with the positional query and field-selector --in. Require exactly one search mode. Compare the stored full title with Python string equality, not display_title, casefold, or Unicode normalization. Return the normal find envelope and mark title as the matching field. Update examples and help without changing storage.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Run focused find tests, then full unittest discovery, tracking check, and git diff --check.

Use the project's ignored TMPDIR for temporary test fixtures, and scoped
support.isolated_discovery only for fixtures that require outside-project
discovery. The repository acceptance commands, run against the implementation
checkout's code and state, are:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check --json
git diff --check
```

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One reviewed implementation commit including documentation and regenerated tracking output.
